title: तीस FIR
logline: Branch A, the night of the doors. Nandini chains her own prisoner to her wrist because he is the only man Imlipur will open a door for, and between twenty past one and ten to ten the two of them turn thirty refused complaints into thirty FIRs on a desk made of their two arms, until the DSP's car pulls up at the thana with the man named in all thirty as chief guest.
language_note: Hinglish: Hindi in Devanagari, English words in Latin script, in the same line.
script_note: Hinglish: Hindi in Devanagari, English words in Latin script

characters.name: नंदिनी जोशी (Nandini Joshi)
characters.role: LEAD. Sub-Inspector, Imlipur thana. Tonight she takes her own prisoner door to door, chained to her, to register thirty FIRs before ten.
characters.look: Indian woman, 28, tall, lean, very straight-backed. Medium-brown skin, oval face, straight thick black eyebrows, a firm mouth that rarely smiles. Low ponytail with a clean centre parting, no loose strands. No make-up, no jewellery, no watch. Approved force uniform, crisp: sandy khaki shirt with two buttoned chest pockets, full sleeves, dark teal epaulettes with TWO off-white bars, white lantern patch on each upper sleeve, khaki trousers, black belt with the handcuff pouch (empty this episode) on her right hip, black shoes, blue ballpoint pen. NO HELMET in this episode (D-016 direction 19). STATE: her LEFT wrist is handcuffed to Nirala's RIGHT wrist from b1 to the end; in a front two-shot she stands picture-left. The green FIR register is under her right arm between doors and open across their two forearms at a door; she writes with her right hand. From b7 a grey cardboard token is in her left chest pocket.
characters.voice_note: Female, late twenties, clear mid-range voice. Educated small-city north-Indian Hindi with crisp English police and office words; the most English-mixed speaker. Quick, clipped. Under pressure quieter, slower, more exact, never louder. Dry, not sarcastic.

characters.name: सुधीर निराला (Sudhir Nirala)
characters.role: Second lead. The fake Inspector, now her prisoner, and the only person the town's doors open for.
characters.look: Indian man, 40, slight and short, narrow sloping shoulders, thin neck. Light-brown skin, long narrow face, large earnest eyes, neat black pencil moustache. Home-stitched copy of the force uniform, over-starched and ONE SIZE TOO BIG: shoulder seams drooping, sleeves to his knuckles, collar standing off his neck, belt tail hanging loose. Teal epaulettes with three off-white bars, lantern patches. THE ONLY PEAKED CAP IN THE SERIES, khaki with a teal band and a shiny black peak, dead level. The palm-wide blank brass medal on its maroon-and-off-white ribbon above his left chest pocket (on all episode). Brown leather holster on his right hip, EMPTY with the flap buttoned flat: the wooden revolver was sealed as case property in s2a01 b2 (S4 confirmed: empty, flap buttoned flat, s2a01 b2 to the end of branch A). STATE: his RIGHT wrist is cuffed to her LEFT; picture-right in a front two-shot. The red cloth-tied file is clamped under his LEFT arm all episode. At a door he holds the open tin ink pad in his free LEFT hand; the pad lives in his right trouser pocket between doors. A few spare grey cardboard tokens on their own short string in his left trouser pocket, carried from habit; the lobby string stays on its nail.
characters.voice_note: Male, forty, light careful tenor. Small-town north-Indian Hindi in an official register, English police terms pronounced with great care. Unhurried, courteous, never raises his voice, never jokes: the comedy is that he means it. Under pressure more formal and quieter, sentences shorter. Says 'madam' at the end of sentences.

characters.name: पुष्पा कुमारी (Pushpa Kumari)
characters.role: Head Constable. Minds the real thana through the night; names the arrivals at the end.
characters.look: Indian woman, 50, short and solid. Wheat-brown skin, round face, sharp small eyes over round steel-rimmed spectacles worn low. Grey-streaked bun with TWO STEEL KNITTING NEEDLES crossed through it. Approved force uniform with ONE off-white bar, lantern patches. Plum-purple hand-knitted cardigan, open, two sagging pockets, orange wool in the right pocket. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Female, fifty, low, dry, even alto. Small-town Hindi, plain and economical. Never surprised. Under pressure slower and more exact. Always 'madam', 'DSP साहब'.

characters.name: अनिल राठौड़ (Anil Rathore), DSP
characters.role: The DSP. First time on screen (b12), stepping out of his white car. No line in this episode.
characters.look: Indian man, 48, tall and lean, upright. Short silver-grey side-parted hair, trimmed grey moustache, rimless rectangular spectacles. Sharply pressed force uniform, teal epaulettes each with ONE BROAD off-white band (no bars, no stars), lantern patches, polished brown belt, slim brown leather cane under his LEFT arm. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Silent in this episode. (Male, late forties, bright, quick, clipped baritone.)

characters.name: बलराम 'भैयाजी' ठाकुर (Balram 'Bhaiyaji' Thakur)
characters.role: Antagonist, named in all thirty FIRs. Arrives in the DSP's car as chief guest (b12). No line in this episode.
characters.look: Indian man, 45, broad and solid, thick neck, big square hands. Thick black hair combed straight back, full black moustache, an unhurried closed-lip smile. Spotless white cotton kurta, sleeves pushed up, white pyjama, brown sandals. Heavy gold watch on his LEFT wrist. Dark sunglasses pushed up on his head, never over his eyes. Fat ring of godown keys on his RIGHT index finger. A marigold welcome garland round his neck (prop, D-016 direction 19). No religious marks, no party colours.
characters.voice_note: Silent in this episode. (Male, mid-forties, warm, low, smiling voice.)

characters.name: रामसेवक (Ramsevak)
characters.role: The first complainant, whose door shut at the end of s2a01. In this episode a hand and a voice only.
characters.look: Never a face in this episode: a thin older man's hand on the edge of a door opened a hand's width, the end of a shawl. The same hand comes down on the ink pad in b4.
characters.voice_note: Tired, flat, older male. One line, half-recognising the knock.

characters.name: शांति देवी (Shanti Devi)
characters.role: Complainant. A one-shot face (b6 shot 1 only); her second line plays over an insert of her hands.
characters.look: Small woman, 65, white hair in a loose bun, green cotton sari, a steel tumbler in her hand.
characters.voice_note: Warm, scolding, grandmotherly. Small-town Hindi, no English.

characters.name: मुकेश (Mukesh)
characters.role: Complainant. A one-shot face (b9 shot 1 only).
characters.look: Young man, late 20s, checked shirt, a folded stamped receipt held up in his fist.
characters.voice_note: Young male, stubborn, hurt. One line.

characters.name: चौथा दरवाज़ा (Door four, voice)
characters.role: A complainant behind a door held on its chain (b10). A hand and a voice; never a face. Not a fourth face.
characters.look: A hand holding a wooden door on its iron chain latch, a hand's width open.
characters.voice_note: Middle-aged, tired, sharp, not unkind; gender is the casting director's call. One line.

location: real_thana (b1, b2, b12); lane_doorway, the one door plate re-dressed per door (b3 to b7, b9 to b11); crossing_stall (b8). No crowd anywhere: the town is hands, thumbs and voices.
time_of_day: Night into morning: 1:20 a.m. in the lockup to 9:55 a.m. in the thana doorway. Night blue with the wall lamp lit (b3 to b6), the lamp going out as the sky greys (b7), dawn at the stall about 6 a.m. (b8), warm morning light from about 7:30 (b9 to b12).

Shot 1 (Pushpa single at the microphone table, the banner behind her, looking past the camera at the yard; this shot establishes the dressed room): the car-door clunk lands at the head of shot 1, before l28; l28. Shot 2 (through the front doorway, past the backs of Nandini and Nirala standing in it, still chained, the register under her right arm, the red file under his left): a white car door open in the yard, the DSP stepping out, cane under his left arm; from the other door, Bhaiyaji in the marigold garland, keys on his finger, smiling; two sheet faces only, the pair are backs. l29 plays over shot 2. sfx_notes: Beds (one ambience per location, from the series library): real_thana night, tube-light hum and a slow ceiling fan; lane night, crickets and a far-off goods train, changing at b7 to first birds and at b9 to a quiet morning town (a distant scooter, a pressure-cooker whistle far away; never voices, never a crowd); crossing_stall dawn, a kettle on a coal stove and the track ticking.
b1: the key grinding in the rusted lock opens the episode over black; then the dry ratchet of the cuff closing on her wrist, close and exposed.
b2: a chain clink as both arms go up; Pushpa's needles set down on the table.

b3: NIRALA'S KNOCK, one fixed rhythm (two slow, one quick), made once and reused in b10, then the door opening a hand's width, all inside the 1.5 s silence before l03; an iron chain latch sliding; a wooden door opening on his last word.
b4: the tin lid of the ink pad; a soft thumb press; pen scratch.
b5: a chain clink on every out-of-step stride; the pen strike in the silence.
b6: a steel tumbler set down on a stone step after l13.
b7: (shot 1 only, the page insert) thumb presses and page turns in a loose rhythm; the wall lamp's buzz dying as it goes out; the first bird.
b8: kettle bubbling, two glasses set down, a chain clink each time his glass lifts. Nothing loud under l32, l17 or l18.
b9: paper unfolding as he holds up the receipt; nothing at all under l20 and l21 but the bed.
b10: the same knock as b3 (two slow, one quick); the door stopping hard on its chain, both inside the 1.5 s silence before l22; the chain sliding off under the end of l25. No effect under l22.

b11: two sets of hurried footsteps, out of rhythm then falling into one; a door shutting; the register cover thumping shut at the head of shot 2, before l27; one chain clink on the salute. The ticking pulse ducks under l33 so 'भैयाजी' lands clean before the b12 car door.

b12: a car idling in the yard, a car door opening (one clean clunk) at the head of shot 1 (the Pushpa single), BEFORE l28, sandals on gravel. The bed and the music duck under l28 and l29; no effect sits on l29, so the cliffhanger stays fully clear. Hold on the tube-light hum and the fan over the final insert.
music_note: Series theme set (bed, tension, sting, ending), instrumental. No music in b1 and b2: the key, the cuff and the chain carry them. From the first knock (b3) a light, warm small-town bed, plucked strings and a soft clarinet, playful under the salute and the goat, ducking under every line. It thins to almost nothing for b9, the turn, and comes back warmer under the dawn tea in b8 and the morning doors. From b11 a ticking pulse joins as the clock runs; it lifts on the salute by choice. On the car door in b12 the pulse stops dead; one low sustained tension note sits under Pushpa's two lines, ducked well below the voice, and a short sting lands on the final insert of her hand, then cut to black.
ending_question: तीसों FIR में जिसका नाम है, वही DSP साहब का chief guest बनकर आया है: DSP साहब register लेंगे, या register के साथ नंदिनी को भी दबा देंगे?
writer_notes: Sources: bible beat_outlines.s2a02 (revision 2), D-006 change 7 (b10, the door she wins herself), D-016 directions 7, 8, 14 and 19, the bible writer_notes for s2a02 b10, and D-013 (state lines, picture-side wording). Ids follow the bible: beats b1 to b12, lines l01 to l29.

Revision 2 (26 Nov), after the critic review in review-notes.json (score 7.9, pass): all four must-fix items and all medium items applied; see writer_response there. l06 now states the target and the clock ('दस बजे तक तीस।'); b11 shot 2 is the salute by choice as its own still (chain SLACK) against b2 shot 1 (chain TAUT); b8 and b9 no longer hold one still past 8 s; b12's zero-time shot and b7's first insert are dropped and the remaining shots renumbered; the knock is 'two slow, one quick' with 1.5 s before l03 and l22; door three's prop is a tin bucket.

Length, counted BY HAND (this session has no shell): dialogue about 943 code points (the critic's 928 plus the 15 added in l06), with spaces and punctuation, without tags or speaker labels, nukta marks stored decomposed. D-016 direction 7 measure is about 1,050. Nothing was added beyond the key lines except one door1_man line (l03, which the bible allows), the carrier on l27 and the target-and-clock clause on l06.

Running time, estimated: spoken targets 108.1 s; 20 speaker changes at 0.3 s = 6.0 s; silences 13.9 s; total 128.0 s, against the 120 aim and the 135 ceiling. Targets average about 8.7 characters a second, slower than the skill's 9 to 10, because the Gate 0b takes ran 20 to 60 per cent over their targets; no line is above 9 a second now (highest l06 at about 8.5).
